shadow:
Something goes wrong inside, a knot of feeling you did not ask for, and the first move the mind makes is to look around the room for who put it there. The weather. The traffic. The person across the table who said the thing. The feeling itself is real and ordinary. The reaching for a cause is where the trouble starts.

Dishonour is what that reaching does, quietly, over years. Each time a mood is handed to someone else to carry, a small lie gets told about where it came from. But the feeling does not actually leave. It goes underground and waits, and the next one piles on top.

Most people treat a hard feeling as a fault in the machine and try to fix it fast. That is the misread. A feeling is not a malfunction. It is weather moving through, and weather only asks to be allowed across the sky. The way out is small and unglamorous. You stop assigning blame for the storm and stand in it as your own. Not approving of it. Just admitting it is yours to feel. That admitting is the whole turn, and it is harder than blame, which costs nothing.
repressive: Some people meet the turbulence by going correct. Everything held, everything polite, the surface smooth as a set table. Underneath, the unspent feeling keeps its own counsel and grows teeth in the dark.
reactive: Others let it out the second it lands, sharp, onto whoever is nearest. It feels like honesty and it feels like justice. It mostly leaves a mess in the room and a private life in pieces.
gift:
Something loosens when a person stops needing the feeling to belong to anyone else. The mood arrives, gets felt, and moves on through without a name tag and without a courtroom. What grows in that cleared space is graciousness.

Graciousness is not manners, though it can look like them from outside. It is closer to a way of carrying yourself through other people. You have done enough honest accounting of your own moods that you no longer leak them onto the room. When someone near you is having a bad day and some of it splashes your way, you can feel for them without picking it up and wearing it. Their state stays theirs. Yours stays yours. The tangle that used to happen just does not happen.

It is like an old floor that was left a little rough, sanded just enough to be soft underfoot. You still get every feeling, the whole range of them, lived all the way down. You simply stop dishonouring them, and stop spending them on people who never agreed to receive them. Life keeps testing this. It is supposed to. Each test is how the thing gets refined, and the refining never quite finishes.
siddhi:
Carried far enough, this stops being something a person practices and becomes the air around them. Grace is the word for it. It is not earned in a single act and it does not announce itself. It tends to fall, the way a good morning falls, unbidden, on someone who happened to be paying attention.

Think of the small lifts that arrive without being summoned. A bird stops you on a path. Light does something to a hillside and the day cracks open for a second. They can only be met, and met more often by a person who has spent years dealing with hardship cleanly, not flinching from the pain, not handing it off.

From here a person can look back at the whole road. The blame, the seething, the feelings shoved underground, the long ledger of who owed what. None of it was a detour. It was the suffering itself, faced and stayed with, that opened the ground for grace to land on. Grace was buried in the shadow the entire time. It only ever asked you to stop hiding.
